newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers, Shaw in pact with @Home.
newsitem.headline: Rogers, Shaw in pact with @Home.

text.p: Canadian cable television companies Rogers Communications Inc and Shaw Communications Inc on Wednesday inked a pact with U.S.-based @Home Network to offer customers swifter Internet access.
The three companies will combine to create WAVE@Home, a high-speed Internet service over cable lines using ultra-quick cable modems.
David Samuel, president of Rogers' WAVE unit, said @Home had deals with hundreds of content providers and could give Internet surfers speedier access to those sites.
Rogers WAVE service connects to the conventional Internet, which slows it from its breakneck pace and can create bottlenecks.
"The analogy we use is a firehose connecting to a bunch of garden hoses," Samuel said in a telephone interview.
Once the transition was complete by the end of this year, Rogers WAVE customers would be connected to another firehose, he added.

Content providers such as CNN, Big Book and 1-800-Flowers plug directly into the @Home network and their information is provided at very high speeds to clients who subscribe to a cable Internet service.
Rogers and Shaw would forge similar deals with Canadian content providers, Samuel said. Other cable companies would also have a chance to provide the service.

"With this new service, Shaw and Rogers will work through the vision.com consortium of cable companies to make the new service available to other cable companies," Shaw President Jim Shaw said in a statement.
Rogers has about 2.2 million customers in Ontario and British Columbia. Shaw has about 1.5 million cable customers, or about 20 percent of the Canadian market.

Both Shaw and Rogers will take an unspecified equity stake in @Home, which is owned by a consortium of U.S. cable TV firms, including Tele-Communications Inc, Comcast Corp, Cox Communications Inc as well as venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers.
Samuel said the amount was not material to Rogers, saying it was "a few million dollars".
